writeup: TIC 201868138 is a candidate eclipsing binary star identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows an orbital period of 3.7158 days with a primary eclipse causing 5.88% dimming of the star's light. A secondary eclipse was also detected at 5.7 sigma significance, located at orbital phase 0.49, indicating the two stars eclipse each other as they orbit. The detection carries a strong signal-to-noise ratio of 237.3 from the Box Least Squares periodogram search, and pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 17.8 and a centroid offset of 2.8 arcsec from the target position. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously uncatalogued system. The automated pipeline assigned this candidate a machine-learning screening score of 0.53, indicating a moderate likelihood that it represents a genuine eclipsing binary.
